title: Branch and Flush
objective: Watch a taken branch flush younger instructions from the 5-stage pipeline, then restructure a loop so that fewer instruction slots are wasted.
explanation:
A conditional branch such as bne rs1, rs2, label compares two registers. If the condition holds, the next PC is the branch target; otherwise it is PC + 4.

Ripes' 5-stage processor keeps fetching sequentially (it effectively predicts not taken) and evaluates branches in the EX stage. When a branch turns out to be taken, the two younger instructions already in IF and ID were fetched from the wrong path. They are squashed (flushed): they never write registers or memory, but they wasted two cycles of pipeline capacity.

The trace records every squashed instruction and links it to the branch that caused it. A loop that branches back on every iteration pays this penalty every time; loop unrolling does more work per iteration and takes fewer branches.
example:
# Mission 3: sum 10 + 9 + ... + 1 with a loop
    addi a0, x0, 0      # sum
    addi a1, x0, 10     # counter
loop:
    add  a0, a0, a1
    addi a1, a1, -1
    bne  a1, x0, loop   # taken 9 times
    addi a2, x0, 1      # code after the loop
    addi a3, x0, 2

steps.title: Catch the first flush
steps.instruction: Clock the processor until the first bne reaches EX and is taken (around cycle 7). The two younger instructions disappear from IF and ID: in the Explorer timeline they are marked as squashed, with the branch as cause.

steps.title: Count the cost
steps.instruction: Run to the end. Check that a0 = 55 and look at the statistics: how many instructions were squashed, and how many branches were taken?

challenge.text: Compute the same sum (a0 = 55) with a loop that still executes at least two conditional branches, but wastes at most 8 instruction slots on flushes (squashed instructions) on the 5-stage processor.
challenge.hint: Unroll the loop: add two counter values per iteration, so the branch is taken half as often.
challenge.reference_solution:
addi a0, x0, 0
    addi a1, x0, 10
loop:
    add  a0, a0, a1
    addi a1, a1, -1
    add  a0, a0, a1
    addi a1, a1, -1
    bne  a1, x0, loop
    addi a2, x0, 1
    addi a3, x0, 2

completion: You measured the cost of taken branches in a pipeline with static not-taken fetching and reduced it with loop unrolling. Real processors add branch predictors to avoid most of these flushes.
